TCU Horned Frogs.oc: Gordon Sammis, in from a successful spell at UConn.
TCU Horned Frogs.oc_status: The guide states this two ways — see the conflicts field. The team pages (pp. 138–139) present Gordon Sammis as arriving from UConn and ask what TCU will look like with him as offensive coordinator, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
TCU Horned Frogs.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator, and the guide refers to coordinator Andy Avalos's group.
TCU Horned Frogs.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
TCU Horned Frogs.offensive_scheme: Named, and changing. The guide flags a real stylistic break: TCU normally runs the Air Raid and Sammis runs a pro-style offense, so this may look nothing like a standard Sonny Dykes team. It records that UConn's offense under him ranked sixth nationally in EPA per play at 0.13 per Game on Paper.
TCU Horned Frogs.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records TCU sitting just outside the top 50 in both EPA per play and Adjusted EPA per play, and says it needs to be nearer the top 25.
TCU Horned Frogs.run_pass: Stated as shifting toward the run. The guide says TCU will lean on a massive offensive line and a good running back group — still throwing, but as a more physical team — and argues the timing could be ideal precisely because Josh Hoover has gone, so spending an hour slinging the ball is no longer an option.
TCU Horned Frogs.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide expects Harvard transfer Jaden Craig to be productive — less aggressive than Hoover, but less mistake-prone and more mobile — with his job being to distribute to playmakers.
TCU Horned Frogs.continuity: The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4 for the head coach, 3 for the offensive coordinator, 3 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 12. The team pages describe the offensive coordinator position differently — see the conflicts field.
TCU Horned Frogs.staff_turnover: The team pages record Gordon Sammis arriving from UConn to run the offense.
TCU Horned Frogs.prior_school: UConn for Sammis. On the roster the guide records Jaden Craig from Harvard, and Josh Hoover leaving for Indiana.
TCU Horned Frogs.portal_recruiting: Not addressed as a staff-driven effect beyond the quarterback replacement.
TCU Horned Frogs.vsin_assessment: Modest on the recent record, alert to the scheme risk. The guide notes Dykes reached the national championship game in 2022 but has had modest results since — a 5-7 hangover in 2023 followed by back-to-back 9-4 seasons. Its summary of the bear case names three things together: a tough schedule, an offensive overhaul that feels a bit ambitious, and uncertainty at linebacker.
TCU Horned Frogs.strengths: A head coach with a national championship game appearance, a coordinator hire whose previous offense ranked sixth nationally in EPA per play, a massive offensive line and good running back group suited to the new approach, a defensive line the guide expects to be a strength and a secondary it calls absolutely loaded.
TCU Horned Frogs.concerns: An offensive overhaul the guide itself calls a bit ambitious — a pro-style system replacing the Air Raid — the loss of a quarterback who threw for nearly 3,500 yards with 29 touchdowns, a linebacking corps made up mostly of first-time starters, and a tough schedule.
TCU Horned Frogs.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-linked warning is that without consistent linebacker play in Andy Avalos's group, the season could disappoint.
TCU Horned Frogs.conflicts: The guide states the offensive coordinator position two ways. The team pages (pp. 138–139) present Gordon Sammis as arriving from UConn and devote a section to what TCU will look like with him in the role, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator. Both are reproduced as printed and neither is corrected.

Texas Tech Red Raiders.dc: Shiel Wood, whom the guide calls a fantastic play-caller.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.play_caller: Shiel Wood on defense, whom the guide says has proven a fantastic play-caller.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the 2025 numbers as exceptional: first nationally in Adjusted EPA per play allowed at -0.25, fifth in yards per play allowed at 5.6, first in havoc rate at 19.3%, and only two teams allowed fewer than 11.8 points per game.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide's reservation about Will Hammond is contextual rather than statistical — Texas Tech was not planning to start him, and handing the keys to a championship-caliber team is a big responsibility.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 3 for 15 returning starters, totalling 13.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Miami (Ohio) transfer Adam Trick as a legitimate star addition.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.portal_recruiting: Treated as the programme's defining advantage and tied directly to the head coach. The guide describes Joey McGuire as fishing with dynamite in the portal, noting Texas Tech has as deep a funding pool as any programme, letting it constantly load up on big-time performers — and this offseason was no different. It records that Brendan Sorsby, one of the portal's biggest prizes, is ineligible this year after being caught betting on sports earlier in his career.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.vsin_assessment: High on the programme and specific about what would undo it. The guide says not to be surprised if Texas Tech cruises to the playoff, and names the two things that could burn them: disappointing quarterback play and the slightest defensive dip. It credits McGuire with liking the young pieces stepping into bigger roles and Shiel Wood with proven play-calling, and expects the defense to be special again.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.strengths: A head coach the guide credits with unmatched portal leverage, both coordinators returning, 15 returning starters, a defensive play-caller the guide calls fantastic coming off a season ranked first nationally in Adjusted EPA per play allowed and first in havoc rate, and a legitimate star portal addition on defense.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.concerns: A quarterback the staff probably wanted on the bench another year or two, inexperienced and coming off a torn ACL; an offensive line that lost two starters including a second-team All-Big 12 guard without clear replacements, which the guide names as one of the few things that could derail the season; and heavy defensive departures including the No. 2 overall pick.
Texas Tech Red Raiders.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

UCF Golden Knights.previous_hc_experience: Yes, at the same programme. The guide records that Scott Frost's first UCF spell took an 0-12 team to 13-0 in two years, and is clear nobody expects a repeat.
UCF Golden Knights.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
UCF Golden Knights.dc_status: Returning — Grinch enters his second season in Orlando, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
UCF Golden Knights.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
UCF Golden Knights.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's conditional expectation is something closer to the 2017 UCF offense, provided the line improves.
UCF Golden Knights.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records UCF cutting from 26.9 points allowed per game in 2024 to 23.6, with the pass defense especially impressive at 185.0 yards allowed per game.
UCF Golden Knights.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
UCF Golden Knights.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide says the quarterback position goes from a mess to a strength with Alonza Barnett III, a high-level dual threat it also describes as a leader and proven winner.
UCF Golden Knights.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 12.
UCF Golden Knights.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
UCF Golden Knights.prior_school: UCF itself for Frost, given his earlier spell. On the roster the guide records Alonza Barnett III from James Madison, Preston Cushman having been at Ole Miss two years ago, and Josh Derry from Monmouth.
UCF Golden Knights.portal_recruiting: Credited as improving. The guide records recruiting and portal work moving in the right direction under Frost, and notes instant-impact signings on defense from both the Group of Five and Power Four.
UCF Golden Knights.vsin_assessment: Improvement credited without inflating it. The guide records Frost winning five games in 2025, improving on the 4-8 season under Gus Malzahn, with recruiting and portal work moving in the right direction, while being clear nobody expects a repeat of 13-0. On the coordinator it notes Alex Grinch's career has been up and down while crediting a very good job last year.
UCF Golden Knights.strengths: A head coach who has already built this programme once, both coordinators returning, a documented defensive improvement with four secondary starters back, a quarterback upgrade the guide calls a move from a mess to a strength, and plentiful skill-position talent.
UCF Golden Knights.concerns: An offensive line that lost four of five starters and which the guide says will still not be one of the better Big 12 units, and a coordinator whose career record the guide describes as up and down.
UCF Golden Knights.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Utah Utes.previous_hc_experience: None as a full-time head coach, though not none in the job. The Coaching Carousel records that Morgan Scalley was basically the head coach-in-waiting for a decade, except for a short period after a scandal involving the use of racial stereotypes, and that he coached the Utes in the Las Vegas Bowl to a 44-22 win before becoming the full-time man.
Utah Utes.oc: Not addressed in guide. The guide records that Jason Beck left for Michigan with Kyle Whittingham.
Utah Utes.dc: Not addressed in guide. Scalley himself was the defensive coordinator for the last 10 seasons.
Utah Utes.oc_status: New — the guide records Jason Beck's departure to Michigan, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Utah Utes.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator, the position Scalley vacated on becoming head coach.
Utah Utes.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Utah Utes.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Utah Utes.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide expects Utah to remain extremely tough to throw against while flagging the run defense as a potential weakness, and traces the knock-on effect — allowing chunk yardage on the ground puts pressure back on the secondary.
Utah Utes.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Utah Utes.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Devon Dampier returning after 2,490 passing yards with 24 touchdowns and only five interceptions plus 835 rushing yards, showing minor accuracy gains in his first Utah season, and is candid about the plan to give Byrd Ficklin snaps, invoking the adage that two quarterbacks means none.
Utah Utes.continuity: Broken on the staff, intact at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 4 for the quarterback, plus 1 for 8 returning starters, totalling 5.
Utah Utes.staff_turnover: Complete at the top, and compounded by what the departing coach took with him: the guide records Whittingham taking offensive coordinator Jason Beck to Michigan along with players including defensive stars John Henry Daley and Smith Snowden.
Utah Utes.prior_school: Utah itself, comprehensively — the Coaching Carousel records that the Salt Lake City native played at Utah and has coached there since 2007, serving as defensive coordinator for the last 10 seasons, and says he certainly knows the programme and is plenty familiar with the recruiting pipelines. On the roster the guide records Cedric Jefferson from Montana State.
Utah Utes.portal_recruiting: Addressed as a retention failure. The guide calls it brutal that Scalley was the coordinator last year and Utah still could not keep Snowden and Henry Daley.
Utah Utes.vsin_assessment: Continuity of person against loss of institution. The guide marks the strangeness of Utah without Whittingham — a two-time Pac-12 Coach of the Year with the programme since 1994 who maintained the standard Urban Meyer set — and says his right-hand man has been tremendous with the defense with no obvious reason not to continue the winning tradition. The Coaching Carousel is measured: it may work out, though year three in the Big 12 might be a little bit rocky.
Utah Utes.strengths: A head coach who played at Utah, has coached there since 2007, ran the defense for 10 seasons, knows the recruiting pipelines and already won a bowl game in charge; a returning dual-threat quarterback with a 24-to-5 touchdown-to-interception season; and a pass defense the guide expects to remain extremely tough.
Utah Utes.concerns: The loss of a coach of Whittingham's standing along with his offensive coordinator and two defensive stars, an offensive line returning no starters at all which the guide says gives no sign of being one of the better Big 12 units, only four returning defensive starters with the line and linebackers shaky, and a two-quarterback plan the guide is openly wary of.
Utah Utes.betting: The guide's three reasons for the Under are stated together and two are about coaching and personnel loss: the loss of a legendary coach, a team that seems weaker in the trenches than usual, and Devon Dampier's arm abandoning him in big games last year.
Utah Utes.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames it as a long-delayed succession: after basically a decade of being the head coach-in-waiting — except for a short period of time after a scandal involving the use of racial stereotypes — Scalley gets his shot with Whittingham off to Michigan. He notes Scalley coached the Utes in the Las Vegas Bowl to a 44-22 win and is now the full-time man. He then sets out the roots: the Salt Lake City native played at Utah and has coached at Utah since 2007, serving as DC for the last 10 seasons, so he certainly knows the programme and is plenty familiar with the recruiting pipelines. His verdict is deliberately provisional — it may work out, though year three in the Big 12 might be a little bit rocky.

West Virginia Mountaineers.previous_hc_experience: Yes, at the same programme — the guide describes 2025 as Rich Rodriguez's return, and this as year two of it.
West Virginia Mountaineers.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
West Virginia Mountaineers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
West Virginia Mountaineers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The guide refers to the offense as the Rodriguez offense.
West Virginia Mountaineers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but attributed to the head coach — the guide says Michael Hawkins should suit the Rodriguez offense.
West Virginia Mountaineers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records West Virginia allowing 30.8 points per game and ranking 64th nationally in Adjusted EPA per play allowed at -0.01, with the pass defense the acute problem at 265.0 yards allowed per game, 129th in FBS.
West Virginia Mountaineers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records the addition of Cam Cook giving West Virginia a running element it lacked.
West Virginia Mountaineers.qb_development: Addressed as scheme fit rather than a record. The guide says Hawkins should suit the Rodriguez offense — clear room to improve as a thrower, but an electric runner who made big plays at Oklahoma.
West Virginia Mountaineers.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 13.
West Virginia Mountaineers.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide beyond the offensive coordinator point printed in the Stability Score table.
West Virginia Mountaineers.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Michael Hawkins from Oklahoma, Cam Cook from Jacksonville State, Jack Cassidy from Western Kentucky, Peter Notaro from Alabama and Bryan Hansen from Colorado.
West Virginia Mountaineers.portal_recruiting: Substantial on offense — the guide records big-time transfer talent added and says the Mountaineers should be harder to stop — and corrective on defense, with bigger corners from smaller programmes and an apparently improved safety group.
West Virginia Mountaineers.vsin_assessment: Balanced on year one, conditional on year two. The guide's read is that 4-8 was not a great season but the team won the Backyard Brawl against Pittsburgh and hung around against good opposition. Its central condition is defensive: unless the unit can get off the field consistently, year two will not be much better than year one.
West Virginia Mountaineers.strengths: A returning head coach with his quarterback and defensive coordinator also back, big-time transfer talent added on offense, an improved offensive line, and a back the guide expects to be among the conference's best.
West Virginia Mountaineers.concerns: A new offensive coordinator, a pass defense that ranked 129th in FBS with a defensive line the guide calls weak, a quarterback it describes as underwhelming as a passer, a receiver group with no clarity on who makes plays on money downs, and unproven kicking and punting.
West Virginia Mountaineers.betting: The guide's lean rests on two specifics, one of them a coaching-adjacent personnel judgement: Michael Hawkins is a good runner but underwhelming as a passer, and the defense needs to be much better after being torched — otherwise the offense would have to be flat-out special, which it doubts.
